questions: If multiple constraints involve the same pair (X_i, Y_i) with different Z_i values, is the instance considered contradictory (thus no solution) or must the values be equal?
Are the indices X_i and Y_i guaranteed to be distinct for each i, or can they be equal, and if they are equal what does the XOR condition imply for A_{X_i}?
Must the output sequence A be printed on a single line, or are line breaks between numbers allowed?
Should the output sequence be terminated with a newline character, and is trailing whitespace after the last number permitted?
Is there any upper bound on the values of A_i beyond being non‑negative integers, e.g., must they fit in 32‑bit signed integers?
When M = 0 (no constraints), is the minimal‑sum sequence defined as all zeros, and should it be output as N zeros?
If the input contains duplicate lines (same X_i, Y_i, Z_i), are they to be treated as separate constraints or can they be ignored?
In the case where the graph of constraints is disconnected, may each connected component be solved independently, and does the minimal sum require any interaction between components?

inline_prompts: You are given integers N, M and three integer sequences of length M: X = (X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_M), Y = (Y_1, Y_2, \ldots, Y_M), and Z = (Z_1, Z_2, \ldots, Z_M). We call a length-N sequence of non-negative integers A = (A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_N) a good sequence if and only if it satisfies the following condition: For every integer i with 1 \le i \le M, the XOR of A_{X_i} and A_{Y_i} is Z_i. Note that the values of A are non-negative integers, and the constraints on their values are not explicitly covered by the given specification; a reasonable competitive-programming default applies, but this isn't the aspect actually left ambiguous here. Determine whether a good sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_N) exists, and if it exists, find one good sequence that minimizes the sum of its elements \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^N A_i. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N M X_1 Y_1 Z_1 X_2 Y_2 Z_2 \vdots X_M Y_M Z_M Output If no good sequence exists, print -1. If a good sequence exists, print one good sequence that minimizes the sum of its elements, separated by spaces. If there are multiple good sequences with the same minimum sum, printing any of them is accepted. Constraints - 1 \le N \le 2\times 10^5 - 0 \le M \le 10^5 - 1 \le X_i, Y_i \le N - 0 \le Z_i \le 10^9 - All input values are integers.

- 0 \le M \le 10^5
- 1 \le X_i, Y_i \le N
